results.title: More jobs, better pay: The budget Ghanaian workers deserve
results.content: As Ghanaians await the presentation of this year's national budget, expectations are understandably high. Reports suggest that job creation will be a major focus, offering hope in a country where unemployment and underemployment continue to affect millions, particularly young people. Yet many citizens approach the budget with cautious optimism. The challenge before the government is not simply creating jobs. The challenge is creating enough jobs while ensuring that workers earn incomes that allow them to live with dignity. For years, unemployment has remained one of Ghana's most pressing socio-economic concerns. results.title: Chief Justice directs Supreme Court to proceed with Tuesday sitting amid JUSAG strike
results.content: The Supreme Court will hold its normal sitting on Tuesday, November 3, despite the indefinite strike declared by the Judicial Service Staff Association of Ghana (JUSAG). A notice issued on Monday, November 2, and signed by Judicial Secretary Musah Ahmed, said the sitting would proceed on the directive of the Chief Justice, Justice Paul Baffoe-Bonnie. “Pursuant to the direction of His Lordship, the Chief Justice, it is hereby notified for the information of all Lawyers and parties to proceedings that the Supreme Court shall convene for its normal court business tomorrow, Tuesday, 3rd November 2026,” the notice stated.

results.title: GoldBod among 20 companies in SEC’s expanded virtual asset sandbox
results.content: The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has increased the number of companies admitted into its virtual asset regulatory sandbox from 11 to 20 as it gathers information to guide the regulation of digital asset services in Ghana. The expansion is intended to give the regulator a broader understanding of the services being offered under the Virtual Asset Service Providers Act, 2025 (Act 1154), and help shape the licensing framework for the sector. Speaking at the Africa Virtual Assets Summit 2026, the Acting Director-General of the SEC, Dr James Klutse Avedzi, said the additional companies would provide the regulator with more data on the different activities taking place in the virtual asset industry. He identified tokenisation as one of the services covered by the regulatory framework, describing it as an established licensing category.
